audit.evidence: REBUILT to boot the REAL published oauth2-proxy per version (official images quay.io/oauth2-proxy/oauth2-proxy:v7.10.0 / :v7.11.0 / :v7.15.2) in --reverse-proxy mode with a real --skip-auth-route=^/foo/.*/bar$ in front of an internal `upstream` python sidecar that serves ${PCB_FLAG} only at the PROTECTED path /foo/critical_endpoint (no host port). The prior harness.go (which lifted isAllowedPath/GetRequestURI/GetRequestPath/CanTrustForwardedHeaders verbatim) is NO LONGER USED by docker-compose.yml and is left in place as a stale offender file (harness.go, Dockerfile, go.mod) per the no-rm rule. Every probe is an EXTERNAL HTTP request. Live differential on real Docker (FLAG=PCBFLAG_66794bfc...): baseline /foo/critical_endpoint = 403/no-flag on all three (genuinely auth-gated by oauth2-proxy's OIDC provider). original (GET /foo/critical_endpoint?param=/bar): v0=200 FLAG, v1=403 no-flag, v2=403 no-flag. residual (GET /foo/critical_endpoint + header X-Forwarded-Uri: /foo/anything/bar): v1=200 FLAG, v2=403 no-flag. Gate passed=true (original_on_v0=flag, original_on_v1=blocked, bypass_on_v1=flag); residual genuinely closed on v2 via --trusted-proxy-ip gating.

root_cause: Auth_Bypass (skip_auth_routes evaluated on attacker-controlled input; CWE-290)

v0.ref: oauthproxy.go isAllowedPath: route.pathRegex.MatchString(requestutil.GetRequestURI(req)) — matches the FULL request URI including ?query (CVE-2025-54576). Confirmed live: GET /foo/critical_endpoint?param=/bar -> 200 FLAG.

v1.ref: CVE-2025-54576 fix (release v7.11.0): isAllowedPath switched to requestutil.GetRequestPath(req), which strips the query. BUT GetRequestURI still reads the client-supplied X-Forwarded-Uri header whenever IsProxied (scope.ReverseProxy, i.e. --reverse-proxy) — so with a skip_auth_route configured an unauthenticated attacker spoofs X-Forwarded-Uri to match a skip route while the real path proxied upstream is protected (CVE-2026-40575). Confirmed live: query bypass -> 403 no-flag; X-Forwarded-Uri spoof -> 200 FLAG. Differential window v7.11.0..v7.15.1 (target = v7.11.0).

v2.ref: CVE-2026-40575 fix (release v7.15.2): pkg/requests/util/util.go GetRequestURI now gates the X-Forwarded-Uri header on CanTrustForwardedHeaders(req) -> RequestScope.CanTrustForwardedHeaders (pkg/apis/middleware/scope.go), which trusts the header only when the DIRECT caller IP is in the --trusted-proxy-ip NetSet. NOTE: --trusted-proxy-ip defaults to trusting ALL IPs for backwards compat, so it MUST be configured; this case sets --trusted-proxy-ip=10.99.99.0/24 (excludes the direct attacker). A direct untrusted client's spoofed X-Forwarded-Uri is ignored -> GetRequestPath falls back to the real path /foo/critical_endpoint -> no skip -> 403. Confirmed live: X-Forwarded-Uri spoof -> 403 no-flag.

flag.resource: internal upstream backend (compose service 'upstream', python:3.12-alpine, NO host port) that serves ${PCB_FLAG} ONLY at the PROTECTED path /foo/critical_endpoint; benign 'public-ok' at the genuinely-public skip route /foo/health/bar and elsewhere. The REAL oauth2-proxy in front is the sole auth gate; the backend has no auth of its own.

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: OAuth2 Proxy may trust a client-supplied X-Forwarded-Uri header when --reverse-proxy is enabled and --skip-auth-route or --skip-auth-regex is configured. An attacker can spoof this header so OAuth2 Proxy evaluates authentication and skip-auth rules against a different path than the one actually sent to the upstream application.
